## What you just did, as diagrams
:::

```{=html}
<div id="m11-explain" class="lx-xgrid">
<div class="lx-fallback">
<dl class="lx-ideas">
<dt>Capital in the goal</dt><dd>Each MW costs its <span class="lx-term" data-term="capital-recovery-factor">capital recovery</span> and upkeep every year: CRF 0.0578 at 4% real over 30 years.</dd>
<dt>Size and hours together</dt><dd>Without a credit the LP builds 22.7 MW: a higher cost per kg than 30 MW, yet more value.</dd>
<dt>A credit in its own years</dt><dd>$3.185 per kg for 10 of 30 years is worth about $1.24/kg over the life: 3.185 × 0.388, the credit years' 38.8% of the discounted kilograms.</dd>
<dt>Why 38.8%, not 47%</dt><dd>The credit years are 47% of the discounted years, but the plant makes 4.96 million kg a year under the tier's cap and 6.91 million after it, when it buys more grid power.</dd>
<dt>A step rule as a set of LPs</dt><dd>One LP per emissions tier, each with a cap on counted grid CO₂ per kg; the top tier wins here, at 46.2 MW.</dd>
<dt>The boundary is part of the answer</dt><dd>The same plant is worth $46.4M as one plant, $121.2M as the electrolyzer's increment, and $63.2M across the grid.</dd>
</dl>
</div>
</div>
```

```{=html}
<div class="lx-deepers">
<details class="lx-deeper">
<summary><span class="k">Go deeper · Modeler</span>The plant's LP in algebra</summary>
<div class="lx-deeper-body">
```

Periods $p$ (the credit's years, then the rest), representative days $d$ with weights $n_d$ (365 in all), hours $t = 0 \dots 23$; MW over an hour is MWh. Money is an annual equivalent in real 2025 dollars:

$$\min\; (\mathit{CRF} + f)\, c\, S \;+\; \sum_p \varphi_p \sum_{d,t} n_d \Big[ (p_t + q)\, \mathit{imp} - p_t\, \mathit{exp} + \big(v - (h + \kappa_p)\, k\big)\, \mathit{ez} \Big]$$

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathit{dw} + \mathit{exp} &\le w_t, \quad \mathit{ez} = \mathit{dw} + \mathit{imp} \le S, \quad \mathit{exp}, \mathit{imp} \le 50 && \text{(each hour)}\\
\textstyle\sum_{d,t} n_d \big(e\, u - L\, k\, \mathit{ez} / 1000\big) &\le 0, \quad u \ge \mathit{imp} - \mathit{exp}, \quad u \ge 0 && \text{(a tier, period 1)}\\
\mathit{dw}, \mathit{exp}, \mathit{imp} &\ge 0, \quad 0 \le S \le 100 && \text{(bounds)}\\
\varphi_1 = \mathit{AF}(r, 10) / \mathit{AF}(r, N), &\quad \varphi_2 = 1 - \varphi_1, \quad \mathit{CRF} = 1 / \mathit{AF}(r, N) && \text{(weights)}
\end{aligned}
$$

| Symbol | Meaning | Unit |
|---|---|---|
| $S$ | the electrolyzer's size (a decision, 0 to 100) | MW |
| $c$ | installed cost: $2,184 per kW = about $2,184,000 per MW | \$/MW |
| $f$ | fixed upkeep: 5% of $c$ every year | share a year |
| $\mathit{dw}$, $\mathit{exp}$, $\mathit{imp}$ | wind to the electrolyzer, wind sold, power bought | MW |
| $\mathit{ez}$ | power into the electrolyzer, $\mathit{dw} + \mathit{imp}$ | MW |
| $p_t$, $q$ | Prairie Town's price, the delivery charge ($10) | \$/MWh |
| $v$ | stack wear, $6.01 per MWh | \$/MWh |
| $h$, $\kappa_p$ | hydrogen price ($4), the credit in period $p$ ($3.185, then 0) | \$/kg |
| $k$ | $1000 / 57$, about 17.54 | kg/MWh |
| $e$, $L$ | the grid's CO₂ rate (0.082), the tier's limit (0.449 for the top tier) | t/MWh, kg/kg |
| $u$ | power bought not matched in the same hour, never below 0 | MW |
| $\mathit{AF}(r, N)$ | annuity factor, $(1 - (1+r)^{-N}) / r$ | years |

- **Bounds matter.** Every power variable is $\ge 0$. Without $u \ge 0$, a negative $u$ in an hour that sells would cancel power bought in another hour: annual matching, not hourly.
- **Two periods, one size.** Period 1 is the credit's 10 years, period 2 the rest of the life; both run on the same 36 days and share $S$.
- **Counting rules.** No certificates: $u = \mathit{imp}$. Annual matching: the cap counts the year's $\sum n_d (\mathit{imp} - \mathit{exp})$ in one row; it may go below zero there, because the right side never does. Across the grid, $\mathit{exp}$ is the wind farm's own sales.
- **Behind one meter**, the plant never buys and sells in the same hour (the tie rule), so hourly matching counts every MWh bought, as no certificates do: the page's LP leaves $u$ out there.
- **Size.** About 5,200 columns and 3,500 rows with a tier; HiGHS solves it in a fraction of a second.

```{=html}
</div>
</details>
<details class="lx-deeper">
<summary><span class="k">Go deeper · Modeler</span>Why one LP per tier</summary>
<div class="lx-deeper-body">
```

- **A step is not linear.** The credit jumps from $0.635 to $3.185 per kg as the rate crosses limits; no single LP can hold the jump.
- **Enumerate the steps.** Each tier fixes the amount and adds one linear cap; five LPs (no credit, four tiers). The largest value wins; of the cases within $1 a year of it, the one listed first.
- **Bound, then skip.** Without its cap, a case's hours are independent once the size is set, so its best value takes a few lines of arithmetic, not an LP. That is a bound. A case needs no LP when its bound falls more than $1 a year short of the best LP so far, or is no better than a case listed before it and already solved, which wins the tie (here, 4 of 5 skipped).
- **The alternative.** A [mixed-integer program]{.lx-term term="mixed-integer-program"} with one binary per tier picks the tier itself ([M2](m02-unit-commitment.html)); it gives no shadow prices, which come only from LPs.
- **What it is not.** The amounts are the law's; the lesson never varies them.

```{=html}
</div>
</details>
<details class="lx-deeper">
<summary><span class="k">Go deeper · Analyst</span>The credit as the IRS states it</summary>
<div class="lx-deeper-body">
```

- **Who.** A facility whose construction begins before 1 January 2028; Public Law 119-21 (2025) ended the credit for later starts. Paid for the 10 years from the day it is [placed in service]{.lx-term term="placed-in-service"}.
- **What.** Hydrogen with at most 4 kg [CO₂e]{.lx-term term="co2e"} per kg, [well-to-gate]{.lx-term term="well-to-gate"}, from DOE's 45VH2-GREET model. 2025 amounts: $0.637, $0.213, $0.159 and $0.127 per kg by tier; five times that with the prevailing wage and apprenticeship rules met.
- **Bought power.** It counts as clean only with [energy attribute certificates]{.lx-term term="energy-attribute-certificate"} from new plants in the same region, matched by year until 2029 and by hour from 2030 (final rules, T.D. 10023, effective 10 January 2025).
- **Simplified here.** One counting rule for all ten years; operating CO₂ in place of the rules' life-cycle grid rate; no taxes, elective pay or transfers.

```{=html}
</div>
</details>
<details class="lx-deeper">
<summary><span class="k">Go deeper</span>What this model leaves out</summary>
<div class="lx-deeper-body">
<ul>
<li>Taxes, depreciation, debt and the financing schedule: the cash flows are the project's, before tax (<a href="a01-project-tea.html">A1</a>).</li>
<li>Compression, storage, delivery and water: DOE's boundary for its cost per kg.</li>
<li>Uncertainty: one weather year, known prices, fixed rules (<a href="m07-monte-carlo.html">M7</a>, <a href="m08-stochastic-robust.html">M8</a>).</li>
<li>Price-taking: the plant's buying and selling do not move Prairie Town's price.</li>
<li>Part-load limits and output that falls with age: the electrolyzer runs anywhere from 0 to its size (<a href="m04-storage-multienergy.html">M4</a>).</li>
</ul>
</div>
</details>
</div>
```

## Check yourself
:::

```{=html}
<div class="lx-myths" data-quiz="m11-myth">
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="window" data-answer="myth">
<p class="lx-qtext">Myth or fact? “A credit of $3.185 per kg is worth $3.185 per kg of the plant's lifetime output.”</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="myth">Myth</li><li data-value="fact">Fact</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Myth. It is paid for 10 of 30 years: levelized over the life it is worth about $1.24/kg here. Counting it every year overstates the NPV by $129.9M.</p></details>
</div>
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="boundary" data-answer="myth">
<p class="lx-qtext">Myth or fact? “Moving the boundary only changes the accounting, never the plan.”</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="myth">Myth</li><li data-value="fact">Fact</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Myth. Taking the increment changes only the accounting (46.2 MW either way), but moving the electrolyzer across the grid changes the plan: 40.1 MW, with every MWh paying the charge.</p></details>
</div>
</div>

<div class="lx-quiz" data-quiz="m11">
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="crf" data-answer="b">
<p class="lx-qtext">A plant costs $100M up front. At 4% real over 30 years, what is its annual equivalent?</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="a">$3.3M</li><li data-value="b">$5.8M</li><li data-value="c">$4.0M</li><li data-value="d">$17.3M</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>$5.8M: the CRF is 0.04 ÷ (1 − 1.04<sup>−30</sup>) = 0.0578.</p><p>$3.3M is $100M ÷ 30 with no interest; $4.0M is interest alone; 17.3 is the annuity factor, in years.</p></details>
</div>
</div>
```

```{=html}
<tbody>
<tr><td class="n">$3.185 per kg</td><td>The hydrogen credit's top tier in 2025 (less than 0.45 kg CO₂e per kg), with the wage and apprenticeship rules met: 5 × $0.637.</td><td class="s"><a href="https://www.irs.gov/instructions/i7210">IRS, Instructions for Form 7210 (2025)</a> · read 6 Nov 2026</td></tr>
<tr><td class="n">before 1 Jan 2028</td><td>When construction must begin for a facility to qualify; the credit then runs 10 years from service.</td><td class="s"><a href="https://www.irs.gov/instructions/i7210">IRS, Instructions for Form 7210 (2025)</a>, What's New · read 6 Nov 2026</td></tr>
<tr><td class="n">0.0578</td><td>The capital recovery factor at 4% real over 30 years: $1 up front equals $0.0578 a year.</td><td class="s">Computed; the formula as in <a href="https://docs.nlr.gov/docs/legosti/old/5173.pdf">NREL's 1995 manual</a></td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</div>
```

```{=html}
<div class="lx-card lx-real">
<p class="lx-eyebrow">In the real world</p>
<blockquote class="lx-excerpt" data-source="excerpt:wind-hydrogen"><p>As the hydrogen price rose, the optimizer built a larger electrolyzer to use more surplus wind.</p><p>The larger unit ran at lower utilization, so each kilogram carried more capital and the levelized cost of hydrogen rose, while hydrogen revenue lowered total system cost.</p><footer>Approved excerpt of: Li et al. (2024), <a href="https://doi.org/10.1115/1.4063971">Journal of Mechanical Design</a>.</footer></blockquote>
<p class="lx-hint">Goal: the lowest life-cycle cost of the whole system, net of what it earns from electricity and hydrogen.</p>
<p class="lx-hint">Where the result holds: one planned 253 MW wind farm in West Texas, with ERCOT wholesale prices; hydrogen sold at a set price per kilogram; cost assumptions dated 2020 to 2023.</p>
<p class="lx-hint">It leaves out: final federal hydrogen credit rules, which came later; the rest of the grid, which enters only through wholesale prices; where the hydrogen goes after it is sold.</p>
<p class="lx-hint">Case file <a href="cf2-cost-per-kg-vs-system-cost.html">CF2</a> tells the study's version: when the cost per kilogram and the cost of the system disagree.</p>
<div class="lx-case-try">
<p class="lx-eyebrow">Try it yourself</p>
<p class="lx-hint">Optional, about 30 minutes; needs Python on your computer (<a href="b02-python-data.html">lesson B2</a>).</p>
<ul>
<li>Run <code>examples/configurations.py</code>: wind, battery, electrolyzer, tank and fuel cell sized and run hour by hour on a synthetic site, with life-cycle costs as present values.</li>
<li>Read “Production incentives” in <code>docs/formulation.md</code>: how does it handle an incentive that lasts fewer years than the analysis period? Compare it with this lesson's two periods.</li>
</ul>
<p><a href="https://github.com/Henryutd2021/reopt-hydrogen-framework">reopt-hydrogen-framework</a>: public example repository · MIT licence · synthetic data.</p>
```
